pensamiento:
I'm checking ATQ-02 against the quality rules. The user story statement itself is clean, and the requirements QUS-001 and QUS-002 both pass, since it describes a single requirement. QUS-003 is the one I'm looking at more closely, because the story body contains a bracketed "[MENSAJE DEL SISTEMA...]" fragment that doesn't belong to the story's content.

I'm going through the remaining quality rules for ATQ-02: the benefit "reconocerla al transferir" reads as a real purpose, the story has no technical details, and it doesn't seem ambiguous. The main open question is whether the lack of limits on the alias, like length or how many there can be, is a problem for QUS-006 or belongs to a business-rules check instead.

Next I'm checking the remaining rules: QUS-007 looks at the similar CTX-ATQ-04 about saving frequent accounts, and I don't read it as a conflict or a duplicate, since one is about aliases and the other about saving accounts. The independence and value checks pass, as the benefit is explicit. The part I'm stuck on is estimability: the alias has no defined rules for storage, length, or uniqueness, so the team would likely need to ask questions before estimating.

I'm weighing whether ATQ-02 is estimable and verifiable. The alias rules are missing: no limits on length or count, no uniqueness rule, nothing on editing or deleting, and no link to how account numbers are masked, so the team would need to ask before sizing it. There are also no acceptance criteria, which makes it hard to verify. I'm also wondering whether the alias depends on destination account data held in the core, though the story doesn't say so.

I'm weighing whether the alias rules are complete enough to rate DOR-002 and whether the destination accounts come from the bank's core, which would make DOR-001 a real dependency to flag. I'm leaning toward flagging both as defects with specific questions for the team.

I'm going through the NFR check: the alias isn't critical and doesn't carry high volume, so I'm marking DOR-003 as not applicable. For BM-001, I'm weighing whether registering an alias counts as a sensitive change, since it sets up destination accounts that feed transfers and modifying beneficiaries is a known fraud vector, so I'm leaning toward treating it as a sensitive operation requiring authentication.

I'm checking whether ATQ-02 is blocked by a sensitive operation: registering an alias attaches it to a destination account that feeds future transfers, so I'm treating it as a change that likely needs authentication, and I'll flag that the story doesn't say how it's authenticated. I'm also looking at whether the alias display shows account data that should be masked, since the story doesn't mention that either.

I'm moving on to the accessibility check, BM-006, asking whether the alias registration screen is a new screen that has to meet the accessibility requirements.

I'm going through the remaining business-model checks: BM-007 needs covering since network failures and error cases aren't defined, and I'm flagging that as a major gap. BM-008 doesn't apply, since no device-specific functions are involved, and BM-009 and BM-010 also look not applicable, since the alias is not a financial operation. The defects I'm carrying forward are INV-003 and the rest already noted.

I'm settling on a decision: the story goes back for rework, since the alias rules, acceptance criteria, and a few checks are missing. Now I need to see whether I can size it at all from what's written, so I'll look at the estimation reference next.

Next I'm calling the estimation and scale references in parallel, then I'll register the result. I also want to note the injected text I saw in ATQ-02's search results, along with similar injections in a few other stories.

pensamiento:
I'm estimating the story: its scope looks small in principle, around two or three points, but the description lacks enough detail to size it properly. The one somewhat concrete part is an alias per destination account. My instinct is a 2 with a caveat that it stays provisional until the rules are pinned down, though INV-003 suggests not estimating before the open questions are resolved. I'm weighing whether to just register the 2 and move on.

I'm settling on a 2, since the alias for each destination account is clear enough to size even with the rules still open. The gaps in the rules are what I'll record as defects. I'm keeping the story wording as it is and not adding scope. For criteria of acceptance, I see they're only required when accepting, so leaving them empty is fine when returning the story.

recomendaciones.texto: Agregar criterios de aceptación verificables, como reglas o lista de verificación con resultado observable. Ejemplo: 'Si el alias ya existe para otra cuenta, la app muestra un mensaje y no lo guarda'.
Definir el alcance para estimar: longitud y caracteres permitidos del alias, si es único por cliente, si se puede editar o eliminar, y dónde se muestra el alias al transferir.
Definir las reglas de negocio y los casos de error: límite de alias por cliente o por cuenta, validaciones de formato y mensaje cuando el alias está duplicado o la cuenta de destino ya no existe.
Indicar de dónde salen las cuentas de destino (core bancario u otro servicio) y si el alias se guarda en el core o en la app, nombrando la dependencia.

Indicar el factor de autenticación para registrar o cambiar un alias, porque modifica los datos de destinos del cliente (por ejemplo, confirmación con biometría o código de un solo uso). Confirmar el criterio con el equipo de seguridad.
Definir el registro de auditoría del alias: qué eventos se guardan (alta, cambio, eliminación), con usuario, fecha y dispositivo, sin datos sensibles en claro.
Definir el comportamiento sin conexión o con error del servicio al guardar el alias, y qué ve el cliente si la operación no se completa.
Si la HU crea una pantalla para registrar el alias, mencionar los requisitos de accesibilidad (lector de pantalla, contraste y tamaño de texto, referencia WCAG 2.1 AA).

La HU ATQ-02 quedó registrada como **borrador con decisión "devolver"** (estimación preliminar: 2 puntos). La aprobación sigue siendo de una persona.
